DE-9IM matrix of any cell

Source: R/cb_predicates.R
cb_matrix.Rd

Look up the DE-9IM intersection matrix of a polygon against grid cells, for a burn with a relations table (see cb_relate()). A cell its boundary touches has its matrix in relations; any other cell is "212FF1FF2" (covered: wholly inside the polygon) if it is in one of the polygon's runs, and "FF2FF1212" (disjoint) if not.

Usage

cb_matrix(x, row, col, id)

Arguments

x

A cb_burn object with a relations table.

row, col

Cell indices (1-based, row 1 at the top), recycled to a common length.

id

Geometry ids, recycled with row and col. May be omitted when the burn has a single geometry.

Value

A character vector of nine-character DE-9IM strings, the polygon's interior, boundary and exterior (rows) against the cell's (columns). NA for cells outside the grid, ids not in the burn, and ids of lines and points (which have no polygon matrix).

See also

cb_cells_where() to select cells by predicate, and cb_materialize(value = "intersects") and friends for dense masks.

Examples

g <- wk::wkt("POLYGON ((1 1, 4 1, 4 4, 1 4, 1 1))")
b <- cb_burn(g, extent = c(0, 6, 0, 6), dimension = c(6, 6), relate = TRUE)
## a cell deep inside, one below the bottom edge (sharing a wall), one
## touching a corner, and one far away
cb_matrix(b, row = c(4, 6, 6, 1), col = c(3, 3, 1, 6))
#> [1] "212FF1FF2" "FF2F11212" "FF2F01212" "FF2FF1212"
